notes.3: The majority of candidates appreciated that the arthropod in the diagram was a myriapod. Option C, insect, was the commonest incorrect response.
notes.4: Many candidates appreciated that the presence of a cell wall and chloroplasts meant that the cell was a plant cell. Some candidates incorrectly opted for the chloroplasts and cell membrane but the cell membrane would be found in both plant and animal cells.
notes.5: This proved to be a demanding question with few candidates appreciating the level of organisation of an ovum and an ovary. The ovum is a cell and the ovary is an organ.
notes.6: Many candidates understood the correct method for working out the actual diameter of the cell. Candidates would benefit from being able to recall and apply the formula for calculating magnification.
notes.7: Most candidates appreciated that in osmosis, diffusion is involved and a partially permeable membrane is required. Some candidates incorrectly believed that cell walls are required for osmosis to occur.
notes.8: This proved to be a very demanding question. Osmosis would cause water to pass through the partially permeable membrane of both pieces of apparatus and so the liquid level in both tubes would rise.
notes.9: Most candidates knew that cellulose, glycogen and starch are the substances made by linking glucose molecules together. Some candidates incorrectly opted for starch, fats and oils.
notes.10: This proved to be a very demanding question. To select the correct option, candidates were required to work through the information on the graph and determine which statement was correct. A methodical approach allowed successful candidates to select option D.
notes.11: Many candidates correctly recalled that enzymes are proteins. Some candidates incorrectly believed that enzymes are made of glucose.
notes.12: There was some uncertainty as to whether the answer was photosynthesis or respiration. Photosynthesis in the spiral-shaped chloroplasts releases oxygen and that oxygen attracts the bacteria.
notes.13: Some candidates found this question challenging with few correctly identifying the spongy mesophyll and the upper epidermis.
notes.14: This proved to be a demanding question. Many candidates did not know that assimilation is the stage of nutrition taking place when food molecules become part of a body cell.
notes.15: Only a small proportion of candidates identified the definition of chemical digestion, that is, large insoluble molecules are changed into smaller soluble molecules.
notes.17: While most candidates understood that water first enters root hair cells, many candidates were uncertain as to whether water then progresses to the xylem or to the mesophyll.
notes.18: Many candidates were uncertain of the name and function of the tissue labelled X. The tissue was the xylem and therefore the function is the transport of water and mineral ions.
notes.19: The features of a vein do not appear to be well known.
notes.22: Many candidates correctly identified where the carbon dioxide concentration was the highest.
notes.23: It was not widely known which processes in the human body require energy from respiration.
notes.24: There was some uncertainty by candidates as to whether the amount of urea in the blood increases as it passes through the liver or the kidney. The liver is responsible for producing urea from excess amino acids whereas the kidneys are responsible for removing urea from the blood.
notes.26: Only a minority of candidates correctly identified the retina as containing cells that are sensitive to light.
notes.31: Many candidates appreciated that both the condom and the diaphragm are barrier methods of birth control. However, some candidates were not aware that the diaphragm is also a barrier method and therefore selected option C.
notes.32: Some candidates did not appreciate that the probability of a couple’s next child being a girl is always 50% regardless of the sex of other children.
notes.34: Many candidates understood that height in humans is best described as continuous variation resulting in a range of phenotypes. However, other candidates were uncertain showing that they did not fully understand the meaning of continuous and discontinuous variation.
notes.39: Many candidates correctly selected option C, but a minority believed that carbon dioxide is used in the making of biofuel and ethanol is used in bread making.
notes.general_comments:
There was good understanding of: the characteristics of living things; white blood cells being the component
of blood that produces antibodies; what is a transmissible disease; the role of testosterone; the sequence of
events when a woman gives birth; the process that produces carbon dioxide from factories and cars, and the
water cycle.
There was some uncertainty about: the characteristics of myriapods; levels of organisation; the features of
osmosis; the stages of human nutrition; the features of a vein; the retina being the part of the eye that
contains cells that are sensitive to light, and the features of mitosis.
It is important for candidates to work methodically through the information provided in the question,
particularly those containing diagrams, such as Questions 8, 10 and 22.
